Team — quick read of ACME's redline: they propose unlimited liability for any confidentiality breach and a separate carve-out referencing "trade secrets as defined under applicable law". We should avoid open-ended uncapped exposure if we can. Proposed approach:

- Accept a carve-out for "willful and material" misappropriation of trade secrets as defined under 18 U.S.C. §1836 (or applicable local statute), with the carve-out limited to actual, provable compensatory damages and injunctive relief (i.e., no punitive or exemplary damages).
- For confidentiality breaches more generally, accept uncapped liability only where we have materially failed to follow our approved security controls and that failure is causal to loss (we can tie to SOC 2 evidence + forensic report).
- Add an incident-handling / evidence timeline in the order form: 30 days for initial forensic report, preservation obligations, and cooperative discovery.

I'll draft redline language; Rishi — can you prepare a short blurb that Rafael can send to Acme that frames this as a customer-friendly compromise (won't slow the deal).

Laura 
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

Rafael / Laura —

Draft blurb below you can send to Acme. I've kept the language pragmatic and tied to objective evidence. Feel free to trim for tone.

--- PROPOSED CUSTOMER-FACING LANGUAGE ---
"The parties agree that the limitation of liability set forth in Section 9 shall not apply to (a) claims arising from the willful and material misappropriation of Customer's trade secrets (as defined by applicable law), or (b) claims arising from a breach of Redwood's confidentiality obligations resulting in unauthorized disclosure of Customer Data, but only to the extent that (i) Customer provides a written forensic report prepared by an independent third party demonstrating that Redwood's proven failure to comply with its applicable security controls was the proximate cause of the unauthorized disclosure, and (ii) Customer seeks only actual compensatory damages and injunctive relief; punitive or exemplary damages remain excluded. In all such cases Redwood's liability shall be subject to documentation and cooperation requirements set forth in the Order Form (including preservation of logs, evidence and a 30-day remediation and assessment period)."

Notes: keeps trade-secret carve-out, ties confidentiality carve-out to independent forensic evidence, and preserves our commercial protections.

Rishi

Julia — following up with proposed compromise we've discussed internally. High level: we're willing to accept a narrowly tailored carve-out for trade-secret misappropriation and confidentiality breaches, provided it's tied to independent forensic evidence and limited to compensatory damages + injunctive relief.

Attached is a clean, customer-friendly paragraph and a tracked-redline version for your counsel (RInfr_Reply_Redline.docx). Key points in plain English:
- Trade secrets: carve-out for willful, material misappropriation (aligned to statutory definition).
- Confidentiality: carve-out only when an independent forensic report shows Redwood materially failed to follow our contractual security controls and that failure caused the disclosure.
- Documentation & timing: we commit to preserve logs and cooperate; customer agrees to provide an independent report within 30 days of discovery.

We think this is a fair compromise that protects Acme's core interests while keeping commercial risk bounded. Happy to jump on call to walk counsel through the intent.
